StackSentry v0.1.0
Target: Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock (Docker 27.3.1, API 1.47)
Scan time: 2026-10-01T12:00:00Z
Rules evaluated: 10 of 10
Containers analyzed: 3 (2 running)
Findings: 4 critical, 2 high, 2 medium, 1 low, 2 info

CRITICAL  SST-HOST-002  docker-01
  The Docker daemon appears to accept API connections over TCP without TLS client verification.
  Evidence: /proc/net/tcp: tcp://0.0.0.0:2375, a process listens on the unencrypted Docker API port
              2375 (reachable from the network)
  Confidence: medium
  Why this matters: The Docker API grants full control over the host. Without TLS client certificate
    verification, anyone who can reach the TCP port can run privileged containers, which is
    equivalent to root access.
  Fix: Remove tcp:// entries from the daemon's -H flags and daemon.json "hosts", or enable TLS with
    --tlsverify and client certificates (port 2376). For remote administration prefer SSH
    (DOCKER_HOST=ssh://user@host) or a VPN.

CRITICAL  SST-HOST-003  watchtower
  A running container was started in privileged mode.
  Evidence: container ID: 222222222222
            privileged: true
  Why this matters: Privileged containers have all capabilities and access to host devices; a
    compromise is close to a compromise of the host.
  Fix: Recreate the container without --privileged / privileged: true and grant only the specific
    capabilities or devices it needs.

CRITICAL  SST-HOST-004  traefik
  A running container has the Docker daemon socket mounted.
  Evidence: container ID: 111111111111
            /var/run/docker.sock -> /var/run/docker.sock (read-only)
  Why this matters: Access to the Docker socket can effectively grant host-level control, even when
    it is mounted read-only.
  Fix: Remove the socket mount unless the container must control Docker. If it must, use a filtering
    socket proxy that only allows the required read-only API endpoints.

CRITICAL  SST-HOST-004  watchtower
  A running container has the Docker daemon socket mounted.
  Evidence: container ID: 222222222222
            /var/run/docker.sock -> /var/run/docker.sock (read-write)
  Why this matters: Access to the Docker socket can effectively grant host-level control, even when
    it is mounted read-only.
  Fix: Remove the socket mount unless the container must control Docker. If it must, use a filtering
    socket proxy that only allows the required read-only API endpoints.

HIGH  SST-HOST-005  watchtower
  A running container shares the host's network namespace.
  Evidence: container ID: 222222222222
            network mode: host
  Why this matters: Host networking removes Docker network isolation; every port the process opens
    is reachable on all host interfaces.
  Fix: Recreate the container on a bridge network and publish only the required ports, preferably
    bound to 127.0.0.1 or a specific interface.

HIGH  SST-HOST-006  watchtower
  A running container has no restart policy and will stay down after a crash or host reboot.
  Evidence: container ID: 222222222222
            restart policy: not set
  Why this matters: Docker's default restart policy is "no". Long-running services without a restart
    policy need manual intervention after failures or reboots.
  Fix: Recreate the container with a restart policy such as unless-stopped (docker update --restart
    unless-stopped <container> also works without recreating it).

MEDIUM  SST-HOST-009  docker-01
  A large amount of Docker disk space is reclaimable.
  Evidence: total Docker disk usage: 32.0 GiB, reclaimable: 26.0 GiB (81%)
            images: 4 using 30.0 GiB (24.0 GiB reclaimable)
            containers: 0 using 0 B (0 B reclaimable)
            volumes: 0 using 0 B (0 B reclaimable)
            build cache: 0 using 2.0 GiB (2.0 GiB reclaimable)
  Why this matters: Unused images, stopped containers, unused volumes and build cache accumulate
    over time. When the filesystem holding Docker's data fills up, containers fail to start, write
    or log.
  Fix: Review docker system df -v and remove unused data with docker image prune, docker builder
    prune and, carefully, docker volume prune. Consider scheduled cleanup and monitoring of the
    Docker data filesystem.

MEDIUM  SST-HOST-010  watchtower
  A running container was created from a mutable image reference (latest or no tag).
  Evidence: container ID: 222222222222
            image: containrrr/watchtower
  Why this matters: Recreating the container may silently pull a different image, which makes
    deployments non-reproducible and rollbacks unreliable.
  Fix: Recreate the container from a pinned version tag, ideally with a digest
    (name:tag@sha256:...).

LOW  SST-HOST-008  docker-01
  The host stores dangling images that are not referenced by any tag.
  Evidence: 1 dangling image(s) using 300.0 MiB
  Why this matters: Dangling images are typically left behind by rebuilds and pulls. They consume
    disk space and are not used by new containers.
  Fix: Remove them with docker image prune after confirming they are not needed.

INFO  SST-HOST-001  docker-01
  The Docker daemon is reachable and its version information was collected.
  Evidence: endpoint: unix:///var/run/docker.sock
            Docker Engine 27.3.1 (API 1.47, linux/amd64)
            host OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS
  Why this matters: Knowing the exact Docker Engine and API version helps to correlate other
    findings with release notes and security advisories for that version.
  Fix: No action required. Keep Docker Engine updated to a supported release.

INFO  SST-HOST-007  docker-01
  The host has stopped containers.
  Evidence: 1 stopped container(s): old-backup
  Why this matters: Stopped containers keep their writable layer and configuration on disk and can
    make it harder to see which workloads are actually in use.
  Fix: Review the stopped containers and remove those that are no longer needed (docker container
    prune removes all stopped containers; review the list first).

Notes:
  - Limitation: No dockerd process is visible in /proc (for example rootless Docker in another
    namespace, Docker Desktop, or restricted /proc); its command line was not checked.
